facts: In real-world action recognition problems, low-level features can not adequately characterize the rich spatial-temporal structures in action videos.
The work encodes actions based on attributes that describe actions as high-level concepts.
The analysis is based on two types of action attributes.
One type of action attributes is generated by humans.
The second type of action attributes is data-driven attributes.
Data-driven attributes are learned from data using dictionary learning methods.
Attribute-based representation may exhibit high variance due to noisy and redundant attributes.
A discriminative and compact attribute-based representation is proposed by selecting a subset of discriminative attributes from a large attribute set.
Three attribute selection criteria are proposed.
The three attribute selection criteria are formulated as a submodular optimization problem.
A greedy optimization algorithm is presented.
The presented greedy optimization algorithm is guaranteed to be at least (1-1 / e) - approximation to the optimum.
Experimental results are on the Olympic Sports dataset.
Experimental results are on the UCF101 dataset.
The proposed attribute-based representation can significantly boost the performance of action recognition algorithms.
